items.caption: 🔌 Connection: The instance runs below an MQTT server/client (splitter) and receives everything HeishaMon publishes. The only mandatory setting is the MQTT base topic - it must match the base topic configured in HeishaMon's own web interface exactly (default of both sides: panasonic_heat_pump). Everything else in this form is optional.
"Debug: unknown topics" writes topics this module does not know yet to the instance debug window - only useful when investigating new firmware topics, leave it off otherwise.

📋 Datapoints: Variables are created automatically as soon as HeishaMon publishes the corresponding topic - the Received column shows what your unit actually sends. Deactivating a datapoint hides its variable (object ID and archive data remain; reactivating simply shows it again); datapoints whose variable does not exist yet are not created while deactivated. Reorder rows by drag & drop - variable positions and links follow the order. "Update variable names" renames only variables that still carry an old default name (your own names stay untouched); "Reset order and selection" restores the default order in the open form - nothing is saved until you click Apply.

🌡️ 1-Wire sensors: Additional temperature sensors (e.g. DS18B20) on the HeishaMon 1-Wire bus are detected automatically at their first reading and appear in their own list for naming and activation - no manual MQTT setup needed.

🔗 Link structure: Creates a grouped category tree (Operation, Heating, DHW, ...) with links to all active datapoints - useful for a tidy WebFront navigation instead of one long flat list. Requires a target category; links of deactivated datapoints are removed automatically.

⚡ External energy meter: If a meter (e.g. Shelly 3EM or an S0 meter wired directly to the HeishaMon board) measures the heat pump supply line, select its power (W) and energy counter (kWh, cumulative) variables. The module then reports the measured electrical power instead of the unit's rough estimate and calculates the measured COP plus the daily performance factor. The minimum power threshold prevents misleading COP values from standby noise. Without an external meter the module uses the unit's own power values; heat pumps of the K/L series and newer report invalid values in the standard power topics, so the module automatically uses the precise values of the extra data block (extra/ topics) as soon as they arrive. If MeterHub already has a meter assigned to function "heat pump", a suggestion with a one-click adopt button appears automatically.

💡 Energy saving check: Assesses the settings received from the unit (DHW target, reheat delta, backup heater enables, heating-off threshold, heating curve, pump duty) and the real cycling behavior (runtime per compressor start) against reference values from the documented HeishaMon example rulesets and the Panasonic service manual. Display only - nothing is changed automatically.

⚙️ Energy saving rulesets: Deploys a parameterized short-cycle guard to the HeishaMon board itself, where it keeps running even if WiFi or IP-Symcon fail. Covers heating by default; "Also protect cooling mode" adds an independent, identical guard on the cool request, since the heat request has no effect while cooling. Deploying replaces the entire ruleset stored on the board; the firmware validates every upload and keeps the previous ruleset on errors.

🔄 Reboot watchdog: If the heat pump stays offline via MQTT for longer than configured, the module triggers a restart of the HeishaMon board via its /reboot endpoint (at most once every 30 minutes). Helps when MQTT hangs but the board's web server still responds; if the board is entirely off the network, its firmware keeps reconnecting on its own.

📊 Archiving: Automatically enables logging for the monitoring datapoints (electrical and thermal power, flow/return/outside temperature, COP, defrost, compressor starts/hours, WiFi quality, MQTT reconnects) so time-series tiles can show day/week/month/year charts. Each variable is activated only once - disabling logging manually in the archive handler is respected permanently.

🆕 Extra commands: Optional switchable variables for the two relays of the large HeishaMon board and the SmartGrid mode (digital replacement for the native SG ready dry contacts; requires the heat pump service setting "Optional PCB" = Yes). Write-only - the displayed value reflects the last command sent, not a confirmation from the unit.

🩺 Board diagnostics: The variable group "Board diagnostics" (WiFi quality, uptime, MQTT reconnects, bus read quality, active rules, firmware version) is fed from the HeishaMon stats topic. When connections drop, its archived history shows the cause: weak WiFi, MQTT hangs, hidden restarts (uptime jumps) or cable/CRC issues.

🤝 Integration: Other NRG-Stack modules (energy management, system schematic, heat pump monitor) find this heat pump automatically via HEISHA_GetFunctions - no manual variable assignment needed. Scripting commands (including reading and setting heating curves and operating functions) and the version history are documented in the README and CHANGELOG of the module; questions and feedback are welcome in the module thread (link in the forum hint below).

Which variable fits as the power source?

popup.caption: Which variable fits as the power source?

items.caption: Select a variable with the CURRENT power draw in watts, measured on the heat pump supply line only (e.g. the heat pump phase of a Shelly 3EM, or the datapoint "S0 meter 1: power" if an S0 meter is wired to the HeishaMon board). Do not select a whole-house meter - the COP would be meaningless. With this set, the module reports Measured=true and calculates the measured COP.

items.name: EnergyVariable
items.caption: Energy meter: energy counter of the heat pump (kWh)
Why must the counter be cumulative?

popup.caption: Why must the counter be cumulative?

items.caption: Select a CUMULATIVE kWh counter (total energy, ever increasing - e.g. the Shelly total counter or the datapoint "S0 meter 1: energy total"). Do NOT select a today/daily value that resets at midnight - the daily performance factor is calculated by this module itself from the counter. The unit must be kWh.

items.name: COPMinPower
items.caption: Minimum power for COP calculation
Why a minimum power threshold?
Below this power, COP (measured) reports 0 instead of a misleading ratio - protects against standby noise (typically a few watts).

elements.caption: ⚙️ Energy saving rulesets (optional, runs on the HeishaMon board)

items.caption: Curated rulesets are uploaded to the HeishaMon board and keep running there autonomously - even if WiFi or IP-Symcon fail. The firmware validates every upload itself; an invalid ruleset is discarded and the previous one stays active.
⚠️ Deploying REPLACES the entire ruleset currently stored on the board. If you maintain your own rules there, do not use this.

items.name: GuardMinOutsideTemp
items.caption: Only above outside temperature
How does the short-cycle guard work?

popup.caption: How does the short-cycle guard work?

items.caption: After each compressor stop, the heat request is lowered for the configured time so the compressor does not restart immediately - fewer starts mean better efficiency and longer compressor life. Below the outside temperature threshold the suppression ends immediately (cold weather takes priority). Template: Compressor-Short-Cycle-Guard from the HeishaMon repository.

items.name: GuardCoolingEnabled
items.caption: 🆕 Also protect cooling mode

items.name: GuardMaxOutsideTempCool
items.caption: Only below outside temperature
Why does cooling need its own guard?

popup.caption: Why does cooling need its own guard?

items.caption: The heat request suppression above has no effect while the unit is cooling - cooling demand is a separate value the heat pump does not touch during heating. This adds an independent, identical suppression on the cool request, so short-cycling is also avoided in cooling mode. Above the outside temperature threshold the suppression ends immediately (hot weather takes priority - mirrors the cold-weather override for heating).
